To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the reconstitution of gelsolin-treated smooth muscle strips with purified actin, Tropomyosin, and Caldesmon restored not only the Ca(2+) -dependent force development but also the Ca(2 +)-induced reduction of cross-sectional area.

the thin filaments of smooth muscle are essential for the Ca(2+) -induced force generation and Ca(2+ )-dependent reduction in muscle cross- sectional area, and that Tropomyosin and Caldesmon are required for the full regulation in addition to the myosin light chain phosphorylation.
the structural remodeling (i.e., removal and reconstitution) of the thin filament is linked to the Ca2+-dependent regulation of smooth muscle function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional roles of the thin filament proteins, Tm and CaM, in the regulation of force generation and muscle CSA in smooth muscle.
the functional roles of the thin filament components in the regulation of Ca(2+ )dependent force generation and muscle shortening in smooth muscle.
the functional roles of the components of thin filament in the regulation of the contractile machinery in smooth muscles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Tm and/or CaD are necessary to regulate smooth muscle contraction, although they may not play an indispensable role.
Tm and/or CaD are necessary to regulate the Ca(2+) sensitivities in the cross-bridge cycling and the actomyosin-based reduction in CSA in smooth muscles.
the regulatory proteins Tm and CaDs are essential for the regulation of smooth muscles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Tm and/or CaD are required for the Ca(2+) sensitization of the actomyosin interaction and the Ca(2+)/CaM-dependent reduction in the muscle CSA.
both the actin and the thin filaments are involved in smooth muscle regulation.

the Ca(2+) regulation of smooth muscle force generation is mediated through the thin filament, and the regulation of the thin filament is mediated through the regulatory proteins, Tm and Ca(2+) in addition to the myosin regulatory system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the thin filaments are the primary regulatory elements in smooth muscle contraction.
the thin filament proteins Tm and CaDs are indispensable for the regulation of smooth muscles.

Tm and/or CaD play an important role in the Ca(2+) regulation of the thin filament structure, which is functionally coupled to the regulation of smooth myosin ATPase activity and the reversible reduction in CSA during smooth muscle contraction.
